title: The head fixation based on skull cap: An improved protocol used in single unit recording in the vestibular system
author: Ren, Li, et al.

steps.title: Select experimental animal
steps.instruction: Use adult chinchillas (C. laniger) weighing 480–550 g.

steps.title: Maintain animal housing
steps.instruction: House each chinchilla individually at 18–23 °C, 65 % humidity, with a 12‑hour light/dark cycle and free access to food and water.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the chinchilla in an airtight box and deliver 5 % isoflurane (liquid) for induction.

steps.title: Maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Switch to a tube face mask and deliver isoflurane at ~2 % (adjustable between 1 %–3 % as needed) for maintenance; the mask also provides mouth fixation.

steps.title: Control core temperature
steps.instruction: Use a DC temperature controller (FHC model 40‑90‑8B) to keep the animal’s core temperature between 36 °C and 38 °C.

steps.title: Monitor vital signs
steps.instruction: Check breathing, heart rhythm, and body temperature every 30 min and adjust isoflurane concentration to avoid over‑anesthesia.

steps.title: Shave head hair
steps.instruction: Trim the hair on the top of the skull to expose the skin.

steps.title: Place animal in stereotaxic chair
steps.instruction: Secure the chinchilla in the animal stereotaxic chair.

steps.title: Preliminary head fixation
steps.instruction: Insert two ear bars into the left and right external auditory canals along the head line for initial fixation.

steps.title: Apply tube face mask
steps.instruction: Position the tube face mask along the animal’s longitudinal axis, push the nasal and incisive bones to lock the incisor teeth against the mask side wall; the mask also delivers anesthesia.

steps.title: Disinfect surgical site
steps.instruction: Apply 0.5 % iodophor to the exposed scalp skin.

steps.title: Provide local anesthesia
steps.instruction: Apply 0.5 % xylocaine to the soft tissues over the skull.

steps.title: Expose skull bone
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, carefully remove skin and underlying tissues over the parietal bones and the posterior half of the frontal bone.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.instruction: Stop any bleeding in the exposed field with electrocautery.

steps.title: Dry bone surface
steps.instruction: Dry the exposed surfaces of the parietal and posterior frontal bones as thoroughly as possible.

steps.title: Apply dental adhesive
steps.instruction: Evenly coat the dried bone surface with a light‑cure universal dental adhesive (OptiBond XTR, model 35,108, USA).

steps.title: Cure adhesive
steps.instruction: Illuminate the adhesive with a UV curing light (Maxima LED RU1200, USA) for 60–80 s.

steps.title: Prepare grip cement
steps.instruction: Mix grip cement powder (CAULK/DENTSPLY, 675,571) with grip cement bulk liquid (CAULK/DENTSPLY, 675,572) to form a sticky fluid compound.

steps.title: Build skull cap
steps.instruction: Apply the sticky cement compound onto the cured adhesive to form a skull cap; immediately embed an 8 mm‑diameter wooden rod into the uncured resin.

steps.title: Cure skull cap
steps.instruction: Allow the dental resin to solidify for about 10 min, securing the wooden rod and creating a rigid bridge between skull and chair.

steps.title: Additional local anesthesia
steps.instruction: Apply 0.5 % xylocaine to the soft tissues over the right mastoid bulla (tympanic cavity).

steps.title: Expose tympanic cavity
steps.instruction: Remove skin and subcutaneous tissue covering the right tympanic cavity to reveal the bone surface.

steps.title: Open tympanic cavity
steps.instruction: Open the top wall of the tympanic cavity to expose the anterior and horizontal semicircular canals, the facial nerve canal, and the petrous part of the temporal bone.

steps.title: Drill fenestra
steps.instruction: Drill a 0.5 mm × 0.5 mm fenestra at the confluence of the anterior and horizontal semicircular canals to expose the superior vestibular nerve bundle.

steps.title: Pull glass micropipettes
steps.instruction: Pull dust‑free glass micropipettes (WPI, model M1B100F-4) using a microelectrode puller (P‑30) to produce glass microelectrodes.

steps.title: Fill microelectrodes
steps.instruction: Fill each microelectrode with 3 mol/L NaCl solution to obtain an impedance of 20–40 MΩ; verify with an impedance meter (SYS‑OMEGAZ).

steps.title: Mount microelectrode
steps.instruction: Attach the microelectrode to a three‑dimensional manipulator (You model US‑3F) fixed on a hydraulic microdrive (Narishige MO‑22).

steps.title: Insert reference electrode
steps.instruction: Insert a PTFE‑coated silver wire (AG10T, needle‑shaped) through the neck skin into the neck muscles.

steps.title: Connect headstage amplifier
steps.instruction: Connect the microelectrode to a headstage preamplifier (resistance 1.1–10 kΩ).

steps.title: Connect extracellular amplifier
steps.instruction: Link the headstage to an extracellular amplifier system (Dagan model 2400A) set to a gain of 500–5000 and a band‑pass filter of 300–3000 Hz.

steps.title: Link to acquisition system
steps.instruction: Connect the extracellular amplifier to the CED Spike2 neural signal acquisition system.

steps.title: Install supporting frame
steps.instruction: Mount the large‑area supporting frame onto the stereotaxic chair (which sits on the gimbaled superstructural platform atop the earth‑vertical rotating table) and align the animal’s longitudinal body axis and head line with the rotation axis.

steps.title: Insert wooden rod
steps.instruction: Place the 8 mm wooden rod embedded in the skull cap into the fixation channel of the supporting frame.

steps.title: Secure rod with screw
steps.instruction: Tighten the screw on the fixation channel wall to lock the rod, creating a rigid bridge between skull and chair.

steps.title: Insert electrode into nerve
steps.instruction: Advance the hydraulic microdrive to drive the glass electrode through the fenestra into the vestibular nerve tissue until a single unit is isolated (extracellular spikes observed).

steps.title: Identify semicircular canal neuron
steps.instruction: Confirm the neuron’s vestibular innervation by monitoring its response to test stimuli; retain only semicircular canal afferent neurons for further experiments.

steps.title: Align rotation plane
steps.instruction: Adjust the gimbaled platform so the neuron’s preferred canal plane coincides with the rotation plane of the rotating table.

steps.title: Apply sinusoidal rotation
steps.instruction: Program the servo‑controlled rate motor (D083M‑22‑1310) to deliver 0.2 Hz sinusoidal rotations at sequential amplitudes of 60, 80, 100, 120, 150, 180, 250, and 300 deg/s; repeat 5 cycles at each amplitude while continuously recording neural activity.
